request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it works**
- **Who made the change:** the server had no way to know who was signed in, so the front end now adds `?user=<name>` to the four requests that change data. A small `byUser` helper in `features/session/session.ts` builds that, and the people and claims screens use it.
- **Writing the line:** each of the four save steps writes its audit line right after the database write succeeds. Those are `BuildPerson` (`PERSON_ADDED`), `SavePerson` (`PERSON_EDITED`), `BuildClaim` (`CLAIM_ADDED`) and `SaveClaim` (`CLAIM_EDITED`). For an edited claim, the server looks up the person's name, since the claim itself only stores the person's id.
- **Format:** amounts are written with two decimals, as the screen shows them, and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. The claim fields are built in one place, `ClaimInput.auditFields`, so added and edited claims always match.

**Refused changes:** a refused change writes nothing. Validation, a duplicate name or a missing record all stop the request before the database write, so the audit line is never reached. This holds for any rule added later too, as long as it fails before or during the save step.

**One thing to know:** the four write requests now require the `user` parameter. Anything other than this screen that calls them without it will be turned away.
